              16.6.3 The Party not prevented from performing its obligations due to the
       Extended Force Majeure Event may at any time terminate this Agreement effective upon
       ten (10) Days’ prior written notice to the affected Party if the affected Party remains
       unable to perform its obligations hereunder twelve (12) Months following the initial
       suspension of performance due to the Force Majeure Event. The twelve (12)-Month
       period need not be continuous if, and only if, each period of suspension of performance
       comprising the twelve (12)-Month period is the result of a common cause such that, if the
       cause had been cured following the first suspension of performance, the additional
       suspensions of performance would not have occurred.

               16.6.4 Upon termination of this Agreement as provided in this Section 16.6, the
       Parties will have no further liability or obligation to each other, except for any obligation
       arising prior to the date of such termination.

       16.7 Effect on Payments. For any period of time when Seller is excused from
providing an amount of Energy due to a Force Majeure Event under Section 16.3, or when
Georgia Power is excused from receiving and purchasing an amount of Energy under
Section 16.3, then (i) such Energy (“Undelivered Force Majeure Energy”) will be included in
Deemed Delivered Energy; and (ii) in no circumstance will such Undelivered Force Majeure
Energy be included in the calculations of the Seasonal Energy True-Up Quantity and Monthly
Delivered Energy in Appendix A.

                           ARTICLE 17: DISPUTE RESOLUTION

        17.1 Dispute Resolution Generally. Either Party (“Disputing Party”) has the right to
give notice to the other Party (“Responding Party”) that the Responding Party is not performing
in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. Such notice (the “Notice of
Dispute”) will describe with specificity the basis for the Disputing Party’s belief and may
describe the recommended options to correct the failure. Within ten (10) Business Days after
receiving the Notice of Dispute, the Responding Party will provide the Disputing Party with a
written notice of each additional issue (if any) with respect to the dispute raised by the Notice of
Dispute, a proposed means for resolving every issue in dispute, and support for such position
(the “Dispute Response”).

        17.2 Initiation of Dispute Resolution; Arbitration. Within five (5) Business Days after
the submission of the Dispute Response, the dispute will be submitted to a designated senior
representative of Seller and a designated senior representative of Georgia Power for resolution. If
the designated senior Representatives are unable to resolve the dispute to the mutual satisfaction
of the Parties within twenty (20) Business Days from the submission to such designated senior
Representatives, or such other period as the Parties may agree upon, then either Party may
provide written notice to the other Party declaring an impasse (the “Impasse Notice”) and
thereafter any such dispute will be resolved in accordance with this Article 17.

        17.3 JAMS. Subject to the limitations of Section 16.4 (Mitigation), and except as
provided in Section 17.10 (Injunctive Relief), any and all controversies, disputes or claims
arising out of, relating to, in connection with or resulting from this Agreement (or any written
amendment hereto), including as to its interpretation, performance, non-performance, validity,

breach or termination, and including any claim based on contract, tort, regulation, rule, statute or
constitution and any claim raising questions of law, whether arising before or after termination of
this Agreement (individually “Claim” and collectively “Claims”) will be resolved under the
Federal Arbitration Act by binding arbitration following the JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration
Rules and Procedures (the “Rules”) of Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services (“JAMS”)

       17.4    Initiation of Arbitration; Selection of Arbitrators.

                17.4.1 Within ten (10) Business Days after delivering an Impasse Notice, the
       delivering Party must contact JAMS to commence arbitration and must provide written
       notice to the other Party in accordance with Section 18.12. Arbitration will be deemed to
       be commenced when JAMS issues a Commencement Letter in accordance with the
       Rules. The Party initiating arbitration will nominate one (1) arbitrator at the same time it
       initiates arbitration. The other Party will nominate one (1) arbitrator within ten (10)
       Business Days of receiving the Commencement Letter. The two Party-nominated
       arbitrators will be deemed neutrals and not the representative of the appointing Party. The
       two (2) arbitrators (the “Party-Appointed Arbitrators”) will appoint a third arbitrator
       (the “Third Arbitrator”). All arbitrators will (i) be competent and experienced in
       matters involving the electric energy business in the United States, with at least ten (10)
       years of legal, engineering, or business experience in the electric industry; (ii) have no
       interest, financial or otherwise, in the Parties or this Agreement beyond payment of their
       fees and expenses for serving on the Arbitration Panel; (iii) have not been previously or
       currently employed or engaged in any capacity other than as a member of the Arbitration
       Panel by Parties, or have a personal or professional relationship with a Party, unless such
       employment, engagement or relationship has been disclosed in writing to all Parties prior
       to the selection of the Arbitration Panel; (iv) not advise or otherwise communicate ex
       parte in any way with either Party following appointment to the Arbitration Panel; and (v)
       treat the details of this Agreement and all Arbitration Panel activity as private and
       confidential, and not publish or disclose any activity without the prior written consent of
       both Parties; further, the Third Arbitrator will be independent of the Parties and the Party-
       Appointed Arbitrators. Each Party will pay the fees and expenses incurred by its Party-
       Appointed Arbitrator and the fees and expenses of the Third Arbitrator will be divided
       equally between the Parties.

               17.4.2 If the Party-Appointed Arbitrators are unable to agree on the Third
       Arbitrator within ten (10) Business Days from initiation of arbitration, then the Third
       Arbitrator will be selected by JAMS with due regard given to the selection criteria above
       and input from Seller, Georgia Power and the Party-Appointed Arbitrators. Parties will
       undertake to request JAMS to complete selection of the Third Arbitrator no later than
       sixty (60) Days from initiation of arbitration. Costs charged by JAMS for this service will
       be borne by the Parties equally.

       applicable state law, federal law, the Federal Arbitration Act, or any other applicable law.
       The Parties hereby waive their right, if any, to recover consequential, special, indirect,
       treble, exemplary, incidental, or punitive damages with respect to this Agreement.

giving rise to the issuance of the injunction.

    Section 18.1.1 will constitute an acceptance and assumption of all obligations by the

                                           APPENDIX A

                   RENEWABLE ENERGY PAYMENT CALCULATION

The Renewable Energy payments to Seller include Monthly Renewable Energy Payments plus a
seasonal true-up payment or credit.

1.       Determination of Monthly Renewable Energy Payments

The Monthly Renewable Energy Payment (“MREP”) will be calculated as follows:

         MREP = MDE * CEP

Where:

         MDE = the Monthly Delivered Energy is the amount of Energy, in MWh, delivered by
         Seller from the Facility to Georgia Power at the Point of Delivery. For the avoidance of
         doubt, all MDE includes the transfer of Environmental Attributes and Electrical Products.

         CEP = the Contract Energy Price for each Annual Period will be as provided in Table A
         below:

                                      2             REDACTED

                                      4             REDACTED

                                      6             REDACTED
                                      7             REDACTED
                                      8             REDACTED
                                      9             REDACTED
                                      10            REDACTED
                                      11            REDACTED
                                      12            REDACTED
                                      13            REDACTED
                                      14            REDACTED
                                      15            REDACTED
                                      16            REDACTED

2.     Determination of Seasonal True-up Payment or Credit

At the end of each Seasonal Period, a calculation will be made to determine whether a true-up
payment or true-up credit is owed for such Seasonal Period as follows: (a) if the sum of the
Monthly Renewable Energy Payments made to Seller for that Seasonal Period is more than the
applicable “Target Seasonal Payment” shown in Table B below, Seller will owe Georgia Power
a true up credit equal to such difference; or (b) if the sum of the Monthly Renewable Energy
Payments made to Seller for that Seasonal Period is less than the applicable Target Seasonal
Payment, Georgia Power will owe Seller a true-up payment equal to such difference. Such true-
up payment or true-up credit will be paid in accordance with Section 10.1.1. For the avoidance
of doubt, (i) any Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy during a Seasonal Period will be
addressed in the Target Seasonal Payment calculation pursuant to the provisions of this
Appendix A, subject to the limitation set forth herein that the Seasonal Energy True-Up
Quantity for the applicable Seasonal Period cannot exceed one hundred and ten percent (110%)
of the applicable Seasonal Energy Contract Amount, and (ii) Georgia Power will receive a
Target Seasonal Payment true-up credit as set forth in Table B if the Seasonal Delivery
Percentage is less than ninety percent (90%), and (iii) Georgia Power will receive a Target
Seasonal Payment true-up credit as set forth in Table B for any amount of Excess Energy that
exceeds ten percent (10%) of the applicable Seasonal Energy Contract Amount.

                                           Table B

     SDP for the Seasonal Period                  Target Seasonal Payment
                                      Winter         Spring        Summer          Fall
                                      Season         Season         Season        Season
                                      100% *         100% *         100% *        100% *
           SDP ≥ 90% FN1              SETQ *         SETQ *         SETQ *        SETQ *
                                        CEP            CEP            CEP           CEP
                                       90% *          95% *          90% *         95% *
         90% > SDP ≥ 85%              SETQ *         SETQ *         SETQ *        SETQ *
                                        CEP            CEP            CEP           CEP


                                   Appendix A – Page 2 of 4

                                                               STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment G PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                     EXECUTION VERSION


                                         80% *          90% *         80% *          90% *
           85% > SDP ≥ 75%              SETQ *         SETQ *        SETQ *         SETQ *
                                          CEP            CEP           CEP            CEP
                                        SETQ *         SETQ *        SETQ *         SETQ *
            75% > SDP ≥ 0%             Prevailing     Prevailing    Prevailing     Prevailing
                                          Rate           Rate          Rate           Rate


Where:

         SDP = Seasonal Delivery Percentage for the applicable Seasonal Period. The SDP is the
         ratio of the sum of the Seasonal Delivered Energy (“SDE”) and any Deemed Delivered
         Energy (“DDE”) to the applicable Seasonal Energy Contract Amount (“SECA”), i.e.,

                SDP = (SDE + DDE) / (SECA)

         SDE = Seasonal Delivered Energy is the amount of Energy, in MWh, delivered by Seller
         to Georgia Power at the Point of Delivery during the applicable Seasonal Period pursuant
         to this Agreement.

         DDE = Deemed Delivered Energy for the applicable Seasonal Period. The methodology
         for the estimate of Deemed Delivered Energy will be determined by the PPA Operating
         Committee. If the Parties fail to agree on the amount of Deemed Delivered Energy, the
         Parties agree to resolve the matter pursuant to the provisions of Article 17.

         SECA = Seasonal Energy Contract Amount for each Seasonal Period will be as provided
         in Appendix H.

         Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy = with respect to a Seasonal Period, any
         Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy during the Seasonal Period determined pursuant
         to Section 8.2.1. The methodology for the calculation of Excess Load Balancing
         Curtailed Energy will be determined by the PPA Operating Committee and will be
         consistent with how Deemed Delivered Energy associated with Georgia Power
         Curtailments is calculated. If the Parties fail to agree on the amount of Excess Load
         Balancing Curtailed Energy, the Parties agree to resolve the matter pursuant to the
         provisions of Article 17.

         SETQ = Seasonal Energy True-Up Quantity for the applicable Seasonal Period. The
         SETQ is the sum of the SDE plus Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy, if any, for
         the applicable Seasonal Period; provided, however, that the SETQ for each respective
         Seasonal Period cannot exceed one hundred and ten percent (110%) of the applicable
         Seasonal Energy Contract Amount. The SETQ will equal the lesser of (i) the sum of the
         SDE plus Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy, if any, for the applicable Seasonal
         Period, and (ii) 110% of the applicable SECA.

                SETQ = Min((SDE FN1 + Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy, if any),
                       110%*SECA)

                                    Appendix A – Page 3 of 4

                                                                         STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment G PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                                EXECUTION VERSION


        For the avoidance of doubt, the amount of Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy (if
        any) included in the calculation of the SETQ for an applicable Seasonal Period cannot
        exceed an amount equal to the difference of (i) 110% of the applicable SECA, minus (ii)
        the SDE, and if the SDE equals or exceeds 110% of the applicable SECA, no amount of
        Excess Load Balancing Curtailed Energy for the Seasonal Period will be included in the
        calculation of the SETQ for the Seasonal Period.

        Prevailing Rate = the lower of AER or 75% of CEP.

        AER = the Avoided Energy Rate will be, for each Hour of a given Month, the amount, in
        $/MWh that is equal to the avoided cost of generation on the Georgia Power territorial
        system for each Hour of such Month as such is calculated by or on behalf of Georgia
        Power pursuant to the RCB Framework approved by the GPSC in Docket No. 40161.

FN1
    Seller may only deliver, and Georgia Power will only receive, Energy that does not exceed the Interconnection
Limit. For the avoidance of doubt, in accordance with Section 6.1.1, this Agreement does not waive or modify any
provision of the Georgia Power Interconnection Agreement with respect to Seller’s ability to deliver energy in
excess of the maximum power output or any limitation on output from the Facility expressed in the Georgia Power
Interconnection Agreement.

                ARTICLE 2: FACILITY DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION

        2.1     Facility. The Facility consists of the solar powered electric generation facilities
with a total capability at the Point of Delivery of seventy-six thousand five hundred (76,500) kW
of electric power, as further described in Appendix E.

       2.2     Consents. Seller hereby agrees to seek to obtain, at its sole expense, any and all
Consents that Seller is required to obtain for the operation, maintenance, testing and any
necessary modification of the Facility.

                         2.2.1      Seller will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, at
          its sole expense, any and all Consents that Seller is required to obtain for the operation,
          maintenance, testing and any necessary modification to the Facility.

                          2.2.2     Georgia Power will use commercially reasonable efforts to
          obtain, at its sole expense, any and all Consents that Georgia Power is required to
          obtain for the purchase of Solar Energy from Seller pursuant to this Agreement.

                          2.2.3      Each Party will support and cooperate with, and not oppose,
          obstruct or otherwise interfere in any means with the efforts of the other Party or its
          Affiliates to obtain all Consents that are the responsibility of that other Party.

                          2.2.4    At the written request of Georgia Power, Seller will use
          reasonable efforts to obtain verification from a certification authority that is mutually
          agreed upon by the Parties, that the Environmental Attributes sold to Georgia Power
          pursuant to this Agreement are in compliance with the standards set by such
          certification authority.

       2.3     Inspections. Upon reasonable prior advance notice to Seller, representatives of
Georgia Power shall be entitled to inspect the construction, maintenance, operation and testing of
the Facility. Seller shall cooperate in such physical inspections of the Facility as may be

reasonably required by Georgia Power provided that: (i) such inspections shall not materially

        2.4      Design and Construction of the Facility. The Facility shall be completed in

use diligent efforts to achieve Commercial Operation of the Facility on or before the Required
Commercial Operation Date and to otherwise carry out its obligations under this Agreement.
The Facility shall be deemed to have achieved “Commercial Operation” upon fulfillment of all
of the following criteria: (i) Seller shall demonstrate that the Facility is capable of producing
Solar Energy and delivering such Solar Energy to the Point of Delivery on a reliable basis in

applicable Consents required under Legal Requirements to be obtained by Seller at the time of
Commercial Operation of the Facility for the construction, ownership, operation and
maintenance of the Facility in accordance with this Agreement.

attributable to (i) a Force Majeure Event, or (ii) the Facility not being interconnected to the

by the Required Commercial Operation Date, Seller shall not have the right to receive any
Monthly Energy Payments until Commercial Operation, and shall pay to Georgia Power
liquidated damages prorated daily as follows until the earlier of the Commercial Operation Date
or the termination date of this Agreement:

                                       Month                $/MWh
                                        1-9                   47

Appendix G is fifteen hundred (1,500) MWh and the Seller fails to achieve Commercial
Operation until one hundred (100) days after the Required Commercial Operation Date, the
liquidated damages would be $47*1500*100/365 = $19,315.

                         ARTICLE 3: TERM AND TERMINATION

        3.1     Term. This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall
remain in full force and effect for a term of thirty (30) Annual Periods (“Term”), subject to the
early termination provisions set forth herein.

        3.2     Survival of Rights. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, the
Parties shall be relieved of their obligations under this Agreement except for the following
obligations that shall survive termination or expiration: (i) the obligation to pay each other all
amounts accrued or then owed and not paid under this Agreement; and (ii) any other obligations
that this Agreement specifically indicates shall survive termination or expiration.

        3.3      Mutual Conditions. The obligations of the Parties under this Agreement are
subject to the satisfaction of each of the following conditions precedent:

                        3.3.1      If required by Legal Requirements, FERC shall have
          approved this Agreement without modification or conditions, or if subject to
          modification or conditions, only such modification or conditions that are acceptable to
          the Parties.

                         3.3.2      If, pursuant to the applicable procedural and scheduling order
          in GPSC Docket No. 36325 (i) the GPSC has not approved this Agreement through the
          granting of a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (“GPSC Certificate”),
          or (ii) the GPSC has issued a Certificate that is subject to material qualifications or
          conditions that adversely affect Georgia Power, then Georgia Power may terminate
          this Agreement upon written notice to Seller; provided, however, that such notice is
          delivered to Seller no later than thirty (30) Days after the issuance of the GPSC Order
          (“GPSC Certificate Target Date”) denying or approving the Certificate with material
          qualifications and conditions. If Georgia Power fails to exercise the aforementioned
          termination right within such thirty (30) Day period, then Georgia Power shall be
          deemed to have waived such termination right. If, within thirty (30) Days from the
          GPSC Certification Target Date, the issuance or denial of the GPSC Certificate has
          been appealed to the GPSC or Fulton County Superior Court, then Georgia Power may
          terminate this Agreement upon written notice to Seller, provided that such notice is
          delivered to Seller no later than eighty (80) Days after the GPSC Certificate Target
          Date. If Georgia Power fails to exercise the aforementioned termination right within
          the applicable notice period, then Georgia Power shall be deemed to have waived such

          revokes the GPSC Certificate with respect to this Agreement (“Amended GPSC
          Certificate”), and the Amended GPSC Certificate imposes material qualifications or

control, operate and maintain the Facility to: (i) comply with all Legal Requirements applicable

          Facility, and (b) Georgia Power complies with rules and regulations of Governmental
          Authorities having jurisdiction with respect to the Facility and with the Seller’s
          reasonable policies and procedures applicable to the Facility including those with
          respect to safety.

                          4.3.1      All such records shall be maintained for a minimum of seven
          (7) years after the creation of such record or data and for any additional period of time
          required by any Legal Requirement or Governmental Authority. In the event Seller
          intends to dispose of or destroy any such records after such seven (7) year period,
          Seller shall provide Georgia Power with thirty (30) Days prior written notice.

                         4.3.2      Seller shall maintain an accurate and up-to-date operating log
          with records of: (i) real power production for each clock hour; (ii) changes in
          operating status and scheduled maintenance; (iii) any unusual conditions found during
          inspections; and (iv) any significant events related to the operation of the Facility.

                         4.3.3     Upon reasonable advance notice, either Party shall have the
          right to examine the records and data of the other Party in order to facilitate any
          determination that such Party is required or permitted to make under this Agreement.

                         4.3.4      Any information provided by either Party pursuant to this
          Section 4.3 shall be subject to the confidentiality provisions set forth in Section 17.16.

                          4.3.5      Georgia Power and Georgia Power’s independent auditor
          shall have the right to inspect from time to time, upon reasonable notice to Seller, such
          books and records of Seller as are reasonably necessary for Georgia Power to
          determine whether Seller constitutes a VIE and the Agreement represents a VI. To the
          extent such inspection requires access to confidential information of Seller, such
          information shall constitute Confidential Information subject to the provisions of
          Section 17.16 of this Agreement.

       4.4     Scheduled Maintenance.

          each calendar year, a schedule of planned Facility outages during which maintenance
          will be performed for the next calendar year (“Scheduled Outages”) (provided that
          Seller shall submit the first such schedule for the first Annual Period no later than
          ninety (90) Days before the commencement of the first Annual Period); provided,
          however, that: (i) Seller shall only conduct Scheduled Outages of the Facility during
          either (a) times that do not occur during a Daylight Period, or (b) a Daylight Period

          occurring in the Months of November or December; and (ii) there shall be no more
          than twenty (20) Scheduled Outage Hours during the total aggregate Daylight Periods
          of any given Month of November or December. Georgia Power shall have thirty (30)
          Days to review the proposed schedule of Scheduled Outages and may approve or

        4.5     Station Service. Seller shall be required to enter into a separate standard retail
agreement with Georgia Power (or another appropriate entity permitted to serve customers at the
Facility’s location) for Station Service not directly provided by the Facility and will be

        4.6     Unplanned Outages. In addition to Scheduled Outages, Seller shall use
commercially reasonable efforts to promptly notify Georgia Power of any event or condition
(other than lack of or variations in sunlight) that will result in the Facility not being able to
produce Solar Energy or a reduction of ten percent (10%) or more in the generating capability of
the Facility, in either case, for more than sixty (60) consecutive minutes, including forced
outages at the Facility and Force Majeure Events affecting the Facility. Such notices shall
contain information describing such event or condition, the beginning date and time of such
event or condition, the expected end date and time of such event or condition, the amount of
Solar Energy that Seller expects will be provided during such event or condition, and any other
information reasonably requested by Georgia Power. With respect to any such event or
condition, Seller shall provide Georgia Power with such notice by any reasonable means required
by Georgia Power, including by telephone or electronic mail.

       4.7      Operating Committee.

          changed at any time by similar written notice. The Operating Representatives shall
          meet as necessary, but not less often than once each calendar year, at a mutually
          agreeable time and place upon prior written notice. The Operating Representatives
          shall represent the Parties in all matters arising hereunder that may be delegated to
          them by mutual agreement of the Parties, but shall not have any authority to modify or
          amend the terms of this Agreement.

                          4.7.2    Each Party shall cooperate in providing to the Operating
          Representatives all information required in the performance of their duties. If the
          Operating Representatives are unable to agree on any matter falling under their
          jurisdiction, such matter shall be submitted to senior officers for discussion and

    4.8    Availability Forecasting.

                      4.8.1       Seller shall provide Georgia Power with forecasts of the
      delivery of energy under this Agreement as described below. Such availability
      forecasts shall include the updated status of all Facility equipment that may impact
      availability. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to forecast the delivery of
      energy under this Agreement accurately and to transmit such information in a format
      reasonably acceptable to Georgia Power. Georgia Power and Seller shall agree upon
      reasonable changes to the requirements and procedures set forth below from time-to-
      time, as necessary to accommodate changes to operating and scheduling procedures of
      Georgia Power.

                     4.8.2     No later than: (i) the earlier of September 1 preceding the
      first Annual Period or forty-five (45) Days prior to the commencement of the first
      Annual Period; and (ii) September 1 of each calendar year for every subsequent
      Annual Period, Seller shall provide to Georgia Power a non-binding forecast of the
      Hourly delivery of energy under this Agreement for an average Day in each Month of
      the following calendar year in a form reasonably acceptable to Georgia Power.

                     4.8.3    Ten (10) Business Days before the commencement of the
      first Annual Period, and thereafter ten (10) Business Days before the beginning of
      each Month during the Term, Seller shall provide to Georgia Power a non-binding
      forecast of the Hourly energy deliveries under this Agreement for each Day of the
      following Month in a form reasonably acceptable to Georgia Power.

                      4.8.4    No later than 5:00 a.m. (Central Prevailing Time) of each
      Day, Seller shall provide Georgia Power a non-binding forecast of energy deliveries
      under this Agreement for the remainder of such Day and the following seven (7) Days
      in a form reasonably acceptable to Georgia Power. Each such notice shall clearly
      identify, for each Hour, Seller’s forecast of all deliveries of energy pursuant to this
      Agreement. In the event that Seller foresees that actual deliveries under this
      Agreement for any Day will be materially different than a forecast previously provided
      for such Day, Seller shall, as soon as reasonably possible, provide notice to Georgia
      Power of such change and an updated forecast. The Operating Committee shall
      determine what constitutes such a material change and identify the Operating
      Representative of Georgia Power that should receive notice of such change.

      The meters shall be of a mutually acceptable accuracy range and type. Seller shall be

of Delivery, and Georgia Power agrees to purchase and receive at the Point of Delivery, one
hundred percent (100%) of the Solar Energy delivered from the Facility, including the transfer of
all Environmental Attributes associated with such Solar Energy. Appendix G provides the
Seller’s expectation of the nominal annual amounts of Solar Energy to be delivered to Georgia

        7.2      Testing and Test Energy and Associated Environmental Attributes. Seller shall

                 ARTICLE 8: MONTHLY ENERGY PAYMENTS

    8.1    Monthly Energy Payments.

                     8.1.1     Georgia Power shall pay Seller a Monthly Energy Payment in
      accordance with Appendix A for Solar Energy delivered to the Point of Delivery by
      Seller (and the Environmental Attributes associated with such Solar Energy) during
      each Month of each Annual Period. After the first Annual Period, if a true-up of the
      Energy Payment Adjustment pursuant to the provisions of Appendix A results in an
      over/under payment during the previous Annual Period, then, following notice by
      Georgia Power of such over/under payment, and unless the Parties agree otherwise,
      Seller shall remit the overpayment amount, or receive the underpayment amount, in
      full from the next succeeding twelve (12) Monthly Energy Payment(s) until such
      over/under payment is satisfied in full.

                   8.1.2    Seller acknowledges and agrees that all price information
      provided by Georgia Power to Seller is Confidential Information subject to Section
      17.16.

                     8.1.3     Provided the Facility has reached Commercial Operation,
      Georgia Power’s obligation to pay the Monthly Energy Payment shall commence on
      January 1, 2017. If the Facility has not reached Commercial Operation by 11:59 p.m.
      Eastern Prevailing Time on December 31, 2016, and the delay is excused pursuant to
      the provisions of Sections 6.1.3 or 15.2, Georgia Power’s obligation to pay the
      Monthly Energy Payment shall commence on the Commercial Operation Date.

                     ARTICLE 9: PAYMENT PROCEDURE

    9.1    Billing and Payment.

                    9.1.1       As promptly as practicable after the end of each Month
      during the Term, Georgia Power shall provide Seller with the meter readings for such
      Month no later than the fifteenth (15th) Business Day of the following Month.

                   9.1.2     Within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of the Monthly
      meter readings, Seller shall provide Georgia Power with an invoice stating the
      Monthly Energy Payment calculated for such Month pursuant to Section 8.1.


                                          25

                                                              STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment D PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                    EXECUTION VERSION
                                                                          2016 ASI PRIME

                    9.1.3      At the option of Seller, Georgia Power will provide a net
      payment or net bill, whichever is applicable, that consolidates amounts owing to Seller
      with amounts owing to Georgia Power.

                     9.1.4      Each Monthly payment shall be due and payable on or before
      the tenth (10th) Day after a Party’s receipt of such invoice. If such tenth (10th) Day
      after a Party’s receipt is not a Business Day, then payment shall be due on the next
      succeeding Business Day. Payment of an invoice shall be made on or before the date
      due in immediately available funds through wire transfer of funds or other means
      acceptable to the Parties. In the event payment is not made on or before such tenth
      (10th) Day, then interest shall be added to the overdue payment, from the date such
      overdue payment was due until such overdue payment together with interest is paid,
      which interest shall be compounded at the Interest Rate.

    9.2    Billing Disputes and Final Accounting.

                     9.2.1      The Parties shall each have until the three hundred sixty-fifth
      (365th) Day after receipt of a Monthly invoice to question or contest the correctness of
      any charge or credit set forth in such invoice. If no question or contest is raised during
      such time period, the correctness of all such charges and credits shall be conclusively
      presumed.

                      9.2.2       In the event a Party questions or contests the correctness of
      any invoiced amount, whether a charge or a credit, of any payment claimed by the
      other Party to be due pursuant to this Agreement, such Party shall provide written
      notice to the other Party (the “Billing Dispute Notice”) that: (i) states the good faith
      basis for the dispute, (ii) specifies the portion of the invoiced amount in dispute, if any,
      and (iii) provides documentation reasonably supporting the determination of the
      disputed amount.

                      9.2.3    In the event that a Party, by timely notice in accordance with
      Sections 9.2.1 and 9.2.2, questions or contests the correctness of any charge or credit,
      the other Party shall promptly review the questioned charge or credit and shall notify
      such Party, within twenty (20) Days following receipt by the other Party of the Billing
      Dispute Notice, of the amount of any error and the amount of any reimbursement, if
      any, that such Party is entitled to receive with respect to such alleged error (the
      “Dispute Review Notice”). Reimbursements determined to be due from a Party under
      this Section 9.2.3 shall be included on the next Monthly invoice and shall include
      interest from the date the original payment was received until the date such
      reimbursement together with interest is invoiced, which interest shall be compounded
      at the Interest Rate.

that there may be legal defenses available to it that are different from or additional to, or
inconsistent with, those available to the Indemnifying Party, the Indemnified Party shall have the
right to select and be represented by separate counsel, at the expense of the Indemnifying Party.
If the Indemnifying Party fails to assume the defense of a claim, the indemnification of which is
required under this Agreement, the Indemnified Party may, at the expense of the Indemnifying
Party, contest, settle, or pay such claim; provided, however, that settlement or full payment of
any such claim may be made only with the Indemnifying Party’s consent or, absent such consent,
written opinion of the Indemnified Party’s counsel that such claim is meritorious or warrants
settlement.

        14.1     Insurance Required of Seller. During the Term, Seller shall acquire and

certifying Seller’s coverage under a liability insurance policy issued by a reputable insurance
company authorized to do business in the state of Georgia naming Seller as a named insured and
Georgia Power as an additional insured.

         14.3     General Terms. Upon commencement of operation of the Facility, the required
insurance coverage shall contain a broad form contractual endorsement specifically covering
liabilities arising out of or caused by the operation of the Facility or by Seller’s failure to
maintain the Facility in satisfactory and safe operating condition. Seller’s insurance must be
primary for all services provided to Georgia Power. Insurance or self-insurance maintained by
Georgia Power or other additional insureds is in excess of Seller’s insurance, contingent and
non-contributory. To the extent allowed by applicable law, Georgia Power, Southern Company
and Affiliates, and each of their officers, directors, employees, representatives, and agents, as
well as each other person or entity so identified in the Agreement, must be additional insured
under the commercial general liability policy. To the extent allowed by applicable law, Seller
waives, and must require its insurers to waive, a right of subrogation against Georgia Power,
Southern Company, and its Affiliates, and each of their officers, directors, employees,
representatives, and agents, for the commercial general liability policy and the workers’
compensation policy.

       14.4    General Liability Insurance. The insurance policy shall provide the following
coverage, which can be exceeded by Seller and may be met through any combination of primary
insurance and following form excess or umbrella insurance as long as the combined limits meet
requirements of this Agreement:

                              ARTICLE 15: FORCE MAJEURE

       15.1    Definition of Force Majeure Event. For the purposes of this Agreement, a
“Force Majeure Event” as to a Party means any occurrence, nonoccurrence or set of
circumstances that prevents a Party, in whole or in part, from performing any of its obligations or

                                                38

                                                                 STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment D PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                       EXECUTION VERSION
                                                                             2016 ASI PRIME

satisfying any conditions under this Agreement and that is beyond the reasonable control of such
Party and is not caused by such Party’s negligence, lack of due diligence, or failure to follow
Prudent Industry Practices. The term Force Majeure Event shall not include: (i) the inability to
meet a Legal Requirement or the change in a Legal Requirement; (ii) a site-specific strike,
walkout, lockout or other labor dispute at the Facility; (iii) equipment failure or equipment
damage, in the case of the Facility only, unless such equipment failure or equipment damage
results directly from an event that would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure Event hereunder;
(iv) changes in market conditions that affect the cost or availability of equipment, materials,
supplies or services, unless such costs or availability changes result directly from an event that
would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure Event hereunder; (v) failures of Seller’s contractors,
suppliers or vendors, unless such failures are caused by an event that would otherwise constitute
a Force Majeure Event if experienced directly by Seller; (vi) unavailability, variability or lack of
adequate solar insolation, unless such unavailability, variability or lack of adequate solar
insolation is caused by an event that would otherwise constitute a Force Majeure Event
hereunder; (vii) Seller’s inability to arrange or maintain transmission/distribution service for
deliveries to the Point of Delivery, unless such inability to arrange or maintain
transmission/distribution service is caused by an event that would otherwise constitute a Force
Majeure Event hereunder; or (viii) any event, including a change in any Legal Requirement or
accounting standard, that results in requiring Georgia Power to consolidate Seller or any of its
Affiliates or permitted assigns as a VIE in Georgia Power’s financial statements.

        15.2     No Breach or Liability. Either Party shall be excused from performance of its
obligations hereunder, other than payment obligations that accrued prior to the declaration of the
Force Majeure Event, and shall not be construed to be in default in respect of such obligations to
the extent that, and for so long as, failure to perform such obligations is due to a Force Majeure
Event.

        15.3    Mitigation. Following the occurrence of a Force Majeure Event, the affected
Party shall:

               (i)    give the other Party notice thereof, followed by written notice if the first
       notice is not written, as promptly as possible after such Party becomes aware of such
       Force Majeure Event, describing the particulars of such Force Majeure Event;

               (ii)     remedy its inability to perform as soon as reasonably practicable;
       provided, however, that this Section 15.3 shall not require the settlement of any non-site
       specific strike, walkout, lockout or other general labor dispute on terms which, in the sole
       judgment of the Party involved in the dispute, are contrary to its interest; and

              (iii) when the affected Party is able to resume performance of its obligations
       under this Agreement, provide the other Party with a written certification from an
       independent, registered engineer that the Force Majeure Event has been cured.

       15.4    Energy Payments. The Monthly Energy Payment and the annual true-up
payment shall be adjusted, in accordance with the provisions of Appendix A, in the event of a
declared Force Majeure Event, a system emergency, or curtailment by Georgia Power or the
Transmission Provider.

                                                39

                                                               STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment D PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                     EXECUTION VERSION
                                                                           2016 ASI PRIME

      15.5    Suspension of Performance. The suspension of performance due to a Force
Majeure Event shall be of no greater scope and of no longer duration than is required by such
Force Majeure Event. No Force Majeure Event shall extend this Agreement beyond the stated
Term.

       15.6    Extended Force Majeure Event.

                         15.6.1    If a Party has reason to believe that a Force Majeure Event,
         which is preventing the other Party from performing its obligations hereunder, will
         result in a suspension of such performance for a term of six (6) Months or longer (an
         “Extended Force Majeure Event”), that Party may request that the other Party submit a
         “Force Majeure Remedy Plan,” which the other Party shall submit to the requesting
         Party within thirty (30) Days of the request. If the Party claiming an excuse under this
         Section 15 has reason to believe that a Force Majeure Event is an Extended Force
         Majeure Event, it shall notify the other Party promptly and shall submit a Force
         Majeure Remedy Plan to the other Party within thirty (30) Days thereafter. The Force
         Majeure Remedy Plan shall set forth a course of repairs, improvements, changes to
         operations or other actions that should permit the affected Party to perform its
         obligations under this Agreement as soon as reasonably practicable.

                        15.6.2   While a Force Majeure Remedy Plan is in effect, the Party
         prevented from performing its obligations due to the Extended Force Majeure Event
         shall provide Monthly status reports to the other Party notifying the other Party of the
         steps that have been taken to remedy the Extended Force Majeure Event and the
         expected remaining duration of the Party’s inability to perform its obligations.

                          15.6.3    The Party not prevented from performing its obligations due
         to the Extended Force Majeure Event may at any time terminate this Agreement
         effective upon ten (10) Days prior written notice to the other Party if: (i) the affected
         Party fails to provide a Force Majeure Remedy Plan as required by this Section 15.6;
         (ii) the affected Party fails to carry out the Force Majeure Remedy Plan in a method
         reasonably designed to cause that Party to be able to perform its obligations hereunder;
         or (iii) the affected Party remains unable to perform its obligations hereunder twelve
         (12) Months following the initial suspension of performance resulting from the Force
         Majeure Event. For the purposes of subsection (iii) of this Section 15.6.3, the twelve
         (12)-Month period need not be continuous if, and only if, each period of suspension of
         performance comprising the twelve (12)-Month period is the result of a common cause
         such that, if the cause had been cured following the first suspension of performance,
         the additional suspensions of performance would not have occurred.

                        15.6.4    Upon termination of this Agreement as provided in this
         Section 15.6, the Parties shall have no further liability or obligation to each other
         except for any obligation arising prior to the date of such termination.

                           ARTICLE 16: DISPUTE RESOLUTION

        16.1     Dispute Resolution Generally. Subject to the limitations of Section 11.5, and
except as provided in Section 16.7, any and all controversies, disputes or claims arising out of,
relating to, in connection with or resulting from this Agreement (or any written amendment
hereto), including as to its interpretation, performance, non-performance, validity, breach or
termination, and including any claim based on contract, tort, regulation, rule, statute or
constitution and any claim raising questions of law, whether arising before or after termination of
this Agreement (individually “Claim” and collectively “Claims”), shall be resolved under the
Federal Arbitration Act by non-binding arbitration following the JAMS Comprehensive
Arbitration Rules and Procedures (the “Rules”) of Judicial Arbitration and Mediation Services
(“JAMS”) then in effect, including its evidentiary and procedural rules, except as modified
herein. It is the Parties’ intent that any arbitration, including the selection and qualification of
arbitrators, shall be conducted in accordance with the Rules, as amended and supplemented,
except where specifically modified by this Agreement, and not by the terms of any state
arbitration act or other Legal Requirement.

       16.2     Initiation of Dispute Resolution.

                         16.2.1     Prior to initiating any arbitration hereunder, a Party wishing
          to make any Claim (“Disputing Party”) shall provide the other Party (“Responding
          Party”) with a formal, written notice of the dispute for each issue in dispute, a
          proposed means for resolving each such issue, and support for such position (the
          “Notice of Dispute”). Within ten (10) Days after receiving the Notice of Dispute, the
          Responding Party shall provide the Disputing Party with a written notice of each
          additional issue (if any) with respect to the dispute raised by the Notice of Dispute, a
          proposed means for resolving every issue in dispute, and support for such position (the
          “Dispute Response”).

                          16.2.2     Within seven (7) Days after the submission of the Dispute
          Response, the Claim shall be submitted to a designated senior representative of Seller
          and a designated senior representative of Georgia Power for resolution. In the event
          the designated senior representatives are unable to resolve the Claim to the mutual
          satisfaction of the Parties within twenty (20) Days from the submission to such
          designated senior representatives, or such other period as the Parties may agree upon,
          then either Party may provide written notice to the other Party declaring an impasse
          (the “Impasse Notice”) and initiating non-binding arbitration in accordance with the
          further provisions of this Article 16.

       16.3     Initiation of Arbitration; Selection of Arbitrators.

                          16.3.1     Arbitration shall be deemed to be initiated when an Impasse
          Notice is given by the delivering Party to the receiving Party in accordance with the
          notice provisions of Section 17.11. The Party initiating arbitration shall nominate one
          (1) arbitrator at the same time it initiates arbitration. The other Party shall nominate
          one (1) arbitrator within ten (10) Days of receiving the Impasse Notice. The two party-
          nominated arbitrators shall be deemed neutrals and not the representative of the

                                                                STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment D PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                                      EXECUTION VERSION
                                                                            2016 ASI PRIME

          appointing party. The two (2) arbitrators (the “Party-Appointed Arbitrators”) shall
          appoint a third arbitrator (the “Third Arbitrator”). All arbitrators shall be competent
          and experienced in matters involving the electric energy business in the United States,
          with at least ten (10) years of legal, engineering, or business experience in the electric
          industry, and shall be impartial and independent of either Party; further, the Third
          Arbitrator shall be independent of the Parties and the Party-Appointed Arbitrators.
          Each Party shall pay for the expenses incurred by its Party Appointed Arbitrator and
          the costs of the Third Arbitrator shall be divided equally between the Parties.

                          16.3.2    If the Party-Appointed Arbitrators are unable to agree on the
          Third Arbitrator within ten (10) Days from initiation of arbitration, then the Third
          Arbitrator shall be selected by JAMS with due regard given to the selection criteria
          above and input from Seller, Georgia Power and the Party-Appointed Arbitrators.
          Parties shall undertake to request JAMS to complete selection of the Third Arbitrator

          this service shall be borne by the Parties equally.

                          16.3.4     If prior to the conclusion of the arbitration a Party-Appointed
          Arbitrator or the Third Arbitrator becomes incapacitated or otherwise unable to serve,
          then a replacement arbitrator shall be appointed in the manner described above and
          applicable to the original arbitrator being replaced.

        16.4    Discovery, Hearing. Discovery and other pre-hearing procedures shall be
conducted as agreed to by the Parties, or if they cannot agree, as determined by a majority of the
Party-Appointed Arbitrators and the Third Arbitrator; provided, however, all pre-hearing
discovery shall be completed within ninety (90) Days following selection of the Third Arbitrator.
Within fifteen (15) Days after completion of such pre-hearing discovery, each Party shall submit
either individually or jointly by overnight delivery to the other Party, the Party-Appointed
Arbitrators and the Third Arbitrator a separate precise statement for each issue in dispute, that
Party’s proposed means of resolving each issue in dispute, and the factual or legal support for
such proposal (the “Proposed Resolutions”). No later than thirty (30) Days after all pre-hearing
discovery has been completed, a hearing shall be conducted at which Seller and Georgia Power
shall each present such evidence and witnesses as they may choose. Arbitration shall be
conducted in accordance with the Rules, as amended and supplemented, except where
specifically modified by this Agreement.

       16.5     Arbitrator Decisions.

                        16.5.1    The Party-Appointed Arbitrators and the Third Arbitrator
          shall consider the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all relevant
          evidence and testimony, and shall render their decision within thirty (30) Days

      16.6    Location of Arbitration.      All arbitrations shall take place in Atlanta, Fulton

        16.7     Injunctive Relief. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article 16, the
Parties acknowledge that an award of damages may not afford complete relief or furnish an
adequate legal remedy as between them, (such as when Seller’s Event of Default arises from
Seller’s actions designed to achieve an economic gain by selling Solar Energy to a third party in
violation of this Agreement). Accordingly, the Parties agree that a Party shall be permitted to
seek at any time, in accordance with applicable laws, procedures, and the terms of this
Agreement, preliminary and permanent injunctive relief relating to the performance of this
Agreement from a Governmental Authority of appropriate jurisdiction, or a court of competent
jurisdiction located in Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia. In the event of entry of any interlocutory
injunctive relief, the party against whom such relief is entered waives the right to have a bond or
security posted pending resolution of the dispute giving rise to the issuance of the injunction.

        16.8    Continued Performance. The Parties agree to continue performing their
respective obligations under this Agreement while the dispute is being resolved unless and until
such obligations are terminated or expire in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.

                                          APPENDIX A

                       SOLAR ENERGY PAYMENT CALCULATIONS

The Solar Energy payments to the Seller include Monthly Energy Payments plus an annual true-
up payment or credit.

1.       Determination of Monthly Energy Payments

The Monthly Energy Payment (“MEP”) shall be calculated as follows:

         If ADP ≥ 75%,         MEP = CEP * MDE * EPA

         If ADP < 75%,         MEP = MDE * Prevailing Rate

Where:

         ADP = Annual Delivery Percentage for the prior Annual Period. The ADP is the ratio of
         the sum of the Annual Delivered Energy (“ADE”) and any Curtailed Energy (“CE”) to
         the Annual Energy Contract Amount (“AECA”), i.e.,

                ADP = (ADE + CE) / (AECA)

         ADE = Annual Delivered Energy is the amount of Solar Energy, in MWh, delivered by
         Seller to Georgia Power at the Point of Delivery plus any Deemed Delivered Energy
         (“DDE”) during the prior Annual Period pursuant to this Agreement.

         CE = Curtailed Energy for the prior Annual Period. In the event a declared Force
         Majeure Event, a system emergency, curtailment by Georgia Power under Section 7.6.1
         or curtailment by the Transmission Provider causes Seller to be unable to deliver Solar
         Energy during the prior Annual Period, the Curtailed Energy shall be the estimated MWh
         that the Parties agree would have been delivered during such events. The methodology
         for the estimate shall be determined by the Operating Committee utilizing the then
         current meteorological data. If the Parties fail to agree on the Curtailed Energy, the
         Parties agree to resolve the matter pursuant to the provisions of Article 16.

         DDE = Deemed Delivered Energy for the prior Annual Period. Deemed Delivered
         Energy is the estimated amount of energy curtailed under Section 7.6.2. The
         methodology for the estimate shall be determined by the Operating Committee utilizing
         the then current meteorological data. If the Parties fail to agree on the Deemed Delivered
         Energy, the Parties agree to resolve the matter pursuant to the provisions of Article 16.

         AECA = Annual Energy Contract Amount for each Annual Period shall be as provided
         in Appendix G.

       EPA = The Energy Payment Adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with Table B
       below based on the ADP for the prior Annual Period. Georgia Power shall apply the
       Energy Payment Adjustment to the Monthly Energy Payment for the duration of the
       current Annual Period. During the first Annual Period of this Agreement such Energy
       Payment Adjustment shall be deemed to be one hundred percent (100%).

                                               Table B
                Annual Delivery Percentage
                                                         Energy Payment
                for the prior Annual Period
                                                           Adjustment
                          (“ADP”)
                         ADP ≥ 90%                           100%
                     90% > ADP ≥ 85%                         90.0%
                     85% > ADP ≥ 75%                         80.0%
                      75% > ADP ≥ 0%                     Prevailing Rate

       Prevailing Rate = the lower of the prevailing CEP or AER.

       AER = the Avoided Energy Rate shall be, for each hour of a given Month, the amount, in
       $/MWh that is equal to the avoided cost of generation on the Georgia Power territorial
       system for each hour of such Month as such is calculated by or on behalf of Georgia
       Power pursuant to the GPSC Orders in Docket Nos. 4822 and 19279.

2.     Determination of Annual True-up Payment or Credit

At the end of each Annual Period, a true-up payment or credit will be calculated to true-up the
total payments made to the Seller during that Annual Period to the annual payment shown in
Table C below (“Target Annual Payment”). The true-up payment or credit shall be equal to the
Target Annual Payment minus the sum of the actual Monthly Energy Payments made to Seller
each Month during that Annual Period.

                                              Table C
         Annual Delivery Percentage for the
                   Annual Period                      Target Annual Payment
                     (“ADP”)
                    ADP ≥ 110%                           Excess ADE Payment
                110% > ADP ≥ 90%                          100% * ADE * CEP
                 90% > ADP ≥ 85%                         90.0% * ADE * CEP
                 85% > ADP ≥ 75%                         80.0% * ADE * CEP
                  75% > ADP ≥ 0%                         Prevailing Rate* ADE

       Excess ADE Payment = the Target Annual Payment in the event the ADP is >= 110% of
       the Annual Energy Contract Amount for the Annual Period shall reflect the sum of:

       1. The Contract Energy Price for 110% of the Annual Energy Contract Amount and


                                   Appendix A Page 3 of 4

                                                         STF-PIA-17-2 Attachment D PUBLIC DISCLOSURE.pdf


PUBLIC DISCLOSURE                                               EXECUTION VERSION
                                                                     2016 ASI PRIME

    2. The minimum of the Contract Energy Price or the average hourly AER for the Annual
       Period for the amount of energy delivered above 110% of the Annual Energy
       Contract amount, i.e.,

       Excess ADE Payment =
       110% * AECA * CEP + Min(CEP,AAC) * (ADE - 110% *AECA)

    AAC = the simple average of the hourly AERs over all hours of the Annual Period.

REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED

Response:
NEER will retain all federal tax credits, as well as any other applicable tax incentives, associated with the Dougherty Solar Project pursuant to the terms of the pro forma Commercial & Industrial Renewable Energy Development Initiative Utility Scale Power Purchase Agreement (“PPA”). Georgia Power does not have access to, nor oversight of, NEER’s tax elections or determinations of tax eligibility related to this project.

===== DKT 56298 & 56310 STF-PIA-17 PD/STF-PIA-17-4.docx =====
STF-PIA-17-4

Question: 
For the Laurens County and Mitchell Solar + BESS projects:
a. Please describe the Company’s current understanding of solar PTC eligibility and PTC phase out.
b. Please describe the Company’s current understanding of solar PTC eligibility and safe harbor requirements. Please describe timing, and actions required for continued eligibility if relying on safe-harbor provisions.
c. Will the Laurens County Solar + BESS project be eligible for solar PTC if it ends up being delayed? How much of a delay could the project face and still retain PTC benefits?
d. Does the Company’s requested certified amount for the Lauren’s County Solar+BESS project estimate assume safe-harbor actions and provisions? If not, why not? What actions would be required to retain safe harbor eligibility?
e. Will the Mitchell Solar + BESS project be eligible for solar PTC if it ends up being delayed? How much of a delay could the project face and still retain PTC benefits?
f. Does the Company’s estimate for the requested certified amount for Mitchell Solar+BESS project assume safe-harbor actions and provisions. If not, why not? What actions would be required to retain safe harbor eligibility?

Response:
To remain eligible for the Production Tax Credit (“PTC”) under the One Big Beautiful Bill (“OBBBA”), solar projects must either start construction by July 4, 2026, or be placed in service by December 31, 2027. Projects that start construction within 12 months of the OBBBA’s enactment (by July 4, 2026) can still qualify for the credits even if completed after 2027, if they meet the four-year continuity safe harbor—meaning they must be placed in service within four years of the year construction began or show continuous construction activity.  The Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) issued guidance on August 15, 2025, that defined “start of construction” as physical work, either onsite or offsite, of significant nature for purposes of qualifying for the federal tax credits under the OBBBA.  
See response to subpart (a). 
Based on the current requirements for PTC eligibility and the project status, delays in the completion of the Laurens County Solar + BESS project could impact the project’s PTC eligibility. The Company anticipates that a commercial operation date (“COD”) beyond 2029 would result in a loss of PTC benefits.  In addition to PTC viability risk, project delays will likely result in increased project costs.increased project costs.
Yes, the Company’s requested certified amount for the Lauren’s County Solar + BESS project assumes the Company will take action to preserve the PTC benefits for the project. As required by the OBBBA and IRS guidance, the project will rely on physical work prior to July 4, 2026, to meet the safe harbor requirements.
Based on the current requirements for PTC eligibility and the project status, delays in the completion of the Mitchell Solar + BESS project could impact the project’s PTC eligibility.  The Company anticipates that a COD beyond 2029 would result in a loss of PTC benefits. In addition to PTC viability risk, project delays will likely result in increased project costs.
Yes, the Company’s requested certified amount for the Mitchell Solar + BESS project assumes the Company will take action to preserve the PTC benefits for the project.  As required by the OBBBA and Treasury guidance, the project will rely on physical work prior to July 4, 2026, to meet the safe harbor requirements.

d. REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED REDACTED
Response:

Response:

===== DKT 56298 & 56310 STF-PIA-17 PD/STF-PIA-17-5.docx =====
STF-PIA-17-5
Question: 
Refer to the original and revised SAM financial models provided in Appendix B.
a. Did the Company assume any capitalization rate for LTSAs? If so, what rate was used, and why was that rate assumed?
b. What assumptions for DOE loan did the Company make for each project. Provide all workpapers for interest rate assumptions and derivation of the revenue requirement savings used in each financial model.
c. How has the Company accounted for DOE loan impacts on interest costs associated with AFUDC and the deemed certified request amounts? Provide all workpapers supporting the derived amounts.
d. How was the Ad Valorem amount calculated for each project? Provide all workpapers supporting the derived amounts. 

Response:
As it relates to thermal Company Owned Proposals (“COPs”), the Company assumes a capitalization rate of 80% for Long-Term Service Agreements (“LTSAs”). This assumption is based on the portion of costs attributed to the purchase of new parts in comparison to all major maintenance costs during the turbine life cycle. Battery energy storage systems (“BESS”) and BESS + Solar COPs have Long-Term Commitments Agreements (“LTCAs”), which provide performance guarantees for energy retention and round-trip efficiency. The LTCA is incremental to the cost to acquire the asset, and an additional guarantee or enhanced measure of the performance of the asset. As such, the performance guarantee is categorized as 100% O&M.  
The Company made appropriate Department of Energy (“DOE”) loan-related assumptions in line with applicable guidance and project eligibility in project SAM files. Approximately 80% of the total investment qualifies for a DOE loan, offering an estimated 1% interest rate reduction. This financing advantage translates to an approximate 5% savings in net present value of revenue requirements. The DOE loan calculation can be found on the ‘Project Inputs’ tab, rows 459-488 calculation can be found on the ‘Project Inputs’ tab rows 459-488. Thermal projects do not include DOE loans. 
The assumed Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (“AFUDC”) debt rate does not account for DOE loan impacts. For impacts to the DOE loan, see response to subpart (b).
Ad valorem tax is calculated based on the gross plant balance for each project. The specific ad valorem tax rate may vary by project depending on its location.

STF-PIA-17-11
Question: 
Refer to the STF-PIA-1-12 Attachment.pdf and the Allocation Methodology and Periodic Rate Computation Procedure Manual, Article IV and Article V.
a. How do Company owned BESS resources factor in to the capacity costs methodology? Please explain.
b. Provide the Company’s last 3 years of IIC contract calculations, including derivation of Capacity Available to Each Operating Company (Section 4.2) and Capacity Rate (Section 5.2).
Response:
Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) resources do not factor into the current capacity cost calculations. BESS resources would not be considered equivalent to traditional peaking facilities or purchased resources when determining the monthly capacity costs for reserve sharing capacity rates. See Section 5.2 of STF-PIA-1-12 Attachment.
Please see STF-PIA-17-11 Attachments A – E, which can also be found at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission eLibrary website at the links included below.

===== DKT 56298 & 56310 STF-PIA-17 PD/STF-PIA-17-10.docx =====
STF-PIA-17-10

Question: 
Refer to STF-1-12 Attachment and the Intercompany Interchange Contract (“IIC”).
a. Is it the Company’s assertion that summer needs can be satisfied through the “IIC”? If not, to what extent does the Company’s modeling support reliance on “IIC”?
b. What is the excess summer position modeled in Aurora through 2031?
c. How are summer firm capacity of solar resources assessed in the IIC? How is the ELCC or reliability assessment performed?

Response:
The Company acknowledges the certification request does not fully meet Georgia Power’s summer capacity needs, but the System has enough resources to cover the summer target planning reserve margin. The Company will pursue the most cost-effective option to maintain system reliability, which could include reserve sharing through the IIC or a contract with an IIC participant, but will also consider other resources. While the System Pool affords IIC participants the ability to rely on temporary surplus capacity on the System, each Operating Company is expected to have adequate resources, including an appropriate level of reserves, to reliably serve its own load obligations. 
Consistent with prior practice, for long-term capacity expansion modeling in the 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (“IRP”) Resource Mix Study (“Mix Study”), the Operating Companies are treated as a system to facilitate coordinated planning and generation additions are added to meet the needs of the system as a whole. 

The scenario expansion plans in the 2025 Mix Study are driven by winter capacity requirements. Meeting winter needs results in sufficient capacity above the target planning reserve margin during the summer. The table below shows the amount of summer capacity above the target planning reserve margin modeled in Aurora for the Budget 2025 MG0 expansion plan.
B2025 MG0 System Expansion Plan Results

The capacity contribution of each resource is based on the effective load carrying capability (“ELCC”) determined by the methodology approved by the Commission in the 2022 IRP filed in Docket No. 44160.


===== DKT 56298 & 56310 STF-PIA-17 PD/STF-PIA-17-9.docx =====
STF-PIA-17-9

Question: 

Would the Company’s EPC contract/agreement allow for the possibility of building just a single 1x1 CC resource at the Bowen site if the Commission were to only approve a single 1x1 CC at the site. Please explain. 

Response:

Yes, the Company’s EPC Agreement with Black and Veatch allows for the possibility of building a single 1x1 CC resource at the Bowen site; however, the Company would be subject to cancellation fees to Black and Veatch.

===== DKT 56298 & 56310 STF-PIA-17 PD/STF-PIA-17-8.docx =====
STF-PIA-17-8

Question: 
Regarding the possibility of self-build resources at the Bowen and/or Wansley sites.
a. Did the Company conduct any evaluations of self-building at those sites? If not, why not? If so, please provide copies of the evaluations performed.
b. Wouldn’t SCS TSS’ familiarity with the sites and contractor diversity be a benefit to self-building at those sites, and wouldn’t reduced costs at those sites also be a benefit, similar to the benefits expected at the McIntosh site?
c. Please explain the difference between McIntosh and Bowen/Wansley sites that resulted in the Company only proposing to self-build at McIntosh.

Response:
The Company did not conduct any evaluations of self-performance at Bowen or Wansley. Please see STF-PIA-10-4, subparts (a) and (d) for additional information.   
Please see the response to subpart (a). 
Please see the response to subpart (a).
